literal: Relocation of Han River refugees to the banks of the Mian. All editions read "Han Province" for "Han River"; at the time there was no "Han Province"—now emended per Yuan gui 486.
idiomatic: Relocation of Han River refugees to the Mian shore. All editions read Han Province for Han River; no such province existed at the time—emended per Yuan gui 486.

literal: Third month, dingsi day; below this there is yichou.
idiomatic: Third month, dingsi day; yichou follows below.

literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on dingmao—there was neither dingsi nor yichou.
idiomatic: That month's new moon fell on dingmao—neither dingsi nor yichou is possible.

literal: Fourth month new moon on bingshen; twenty-second day dingsi, thirtieth day yichou.
idiomatic: Fourth month: new moon on bingshen; dingsi on the twenty-second day, yichou on the thirtieth.

literal: Zizhi tongjian Collation says: "According to the long calendar, second month new moon on renchen; tenth day xinchou, twentieth day xinhai.
idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian Collation notes: "Per the long calendar, second-month new moon on renchen; xinchou on the tenth day, xinhai on the twentieth.

literal: General Who Pacifies the North Jun, Prince of Wuling, Governor of Xu and Yan provinces, demoted to General Who Pacifies the Army. "Jun" in the Song edition reads tabooed character.
idiomatic: Prince of Wuling Jun, General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Xu and Yan, demoted to General Who Pacifies the Army. The Song edition has a taboo placeholder for Jun.

literal: The Sanzhao edition, Northern Directorate edition, Mao edition, and Hall edition read "Zan"; now corrected per the Basic Annals of Emperor Xiaowu.
idiomatic: The Sanzhao, Northern Directorate, Mao, and Hall editions read Zan; corrected per Emperor Xiaowu's annals.

literal: See collation note 30 in this juan.
idiomatic: See collation note 30 in this scroll.

literal: Fifth month yiyou: the outlaw Sima Shunze styled himself King of Qi and seized Liangzou; dingsi: Pohuang kingdom; wuxu: Prince of Henan; all sent tribute. According to the calendar, that year fifth month new moon was on jiashen; second day yiyou, fifteenth day wuxu—there was no dingsi.
idiomatic: On yiyou of the fifth month, outlaw Sima Shunze declared himself King of Qi and held Liangzou; entries for dingsi (Pohuang), wuxu (Prince of Henan), and tribute missions follow. That year's fifth month began on jiashen—yiyou was day 2, wuxu day 15; dingsi cannot occur.

literal: The dingsi day entry is surely in error.
idiomatic: The dingsi entry must be corrupt.

literal: "Could not yet establish their livelihoods": all editions read "could not yet" for "establish"; now emended per Yuan gui 195.
idiomatic: "Households had not yet established livelihoods": all editions read neng (able) for li (establish)—emended per Yuan gui 195.

literal: Wuwu. All editions read gengwu; now changed per the History of the Southern Dynasties.
idiomatic: Wuwu day. All editions read gengwu; emended per Nanshi.

literal: According to the calendar, that month had new moon on gengxu—there was no gengwu.
idiomatic: That month opened on gengxu—gengwu is impossible.
Wuwu fell on the ninth day.
